rows.text: returns at once when qword `[rcx]` equals qword `[rcx+8]`; otherwise walks the qword slots from `[rcx]` while the cursor differs from qword `[rcx+8]`, calling the function at `001B6B50` + 0x23 with each slot's qword: when it returns non-zero (`al`) and the next slot is below qword `[rcx+8]` (unsigned) it makes the indirect call at `001B6B50` + 0x3E with the current slot, the next slot and the byte count from the next slot to `[rcx+8]`, then subtracts 8 from qword `[rcx+8]` without advancing the cursor; when it returns 0 the cursor advances 8
tail-jumps at `002DF170` + 0xC with `ecx` = 1, `edx` = the incoming `ecx`, `r8d` = 0 and `r9d` = the incoming `edx`

returns at once when `rcx` is null; otherwise walks 16 qword slots of `rcx` (index below 0x10, signed) and for each non-null slot whose byte `+0x11` equals `dl` calls the functions at `003339C0` + 0x42 and `003339C0` + 0x4A with that slot's pointer and stores 0 in the slot; after the loop calls the function at `003339C0` + 0x60 with `dl` zero-extended

walks the node list starting at qword `+8` of qword `02EBEF88` (next link qword `+8`), doing nothing when it is null; in each node it replaces qword `+0x100` and qword `+0x108` with `rdx` where they equal `rcx`, then walks the chain from qword `+0x118` (next link qword `+0x30`), replacing qword `+0x18` with `rdx` when it equals `rcx`, or else qword `+0x20` when that equals `rcx`

returns at once when dword `rcx+0xC4` is -1; otherwise calls the function at `00424040` + 0x15 with dword `rcx+0x10`, then the function at `00424040` + 0x27 with qword `+0xDA8` of that result and dword `rcx+0xC4`, and when that returns non-null ORs 0x40 into its dword `+0xC`
stores word 0 at `rcx+0xC`, word 1 at `rcx+2` and byte 1 at `[rcx]`
returns at once when byte `[rcx]` is non-zero; otherwise copies dword `rcx+0x10` to `+0x18` and dword `+0x14` to `+0x1C`, stores dword 0x101 at `[rcx]` and dword `0x3f800000` at `+0xC`
clears bit 0x20 and sets bit 0x10 of byte `rcx+9`; then, only when that byte is below 0x40 (unsigned) and byte `+8` is 0, stores qword 8 at `+0x10`, word 1 at `+0xA` and byte 1 at `+8`
reads byte `rcx+0x34`; when its bit 0 is already set returns with that byte in `eax`, otherwise sets bit 0, stores word 0 at `+0x30` and returns 0
